Incident review 2030-05-14 High

Checkout failed for 47 minutes after a certificate expired

The certificate of the payment gateway's internal endpoint expired at 10:42 UTC, so POST /checkout failed; every customer saw it until a new one was issued. See the runbook.

Authors: Payments team

Impact

Duration
47 minutes
Failed checkouts
about 3,100
Customers affected
all, in every region
Data lost
none

Timeline

  1. 2030-05-14 10:42
    The certificate expires
  2. 10:44
    Checkout errors cross the alert threshold

    The on-call engineer is paged.

  3. 10:58
    Cause found

    TLS handshake failures in the gateway's logs point at the certificate.

  4. 11:21
    A new certificate is issued and deployed
  5. 11:29
    Checkout recovers
  6. 2030-05-15 09:00
    Review held

Cause

The certificate was issued by hand two years ago and was not in the renewal job's list, so nothing renewed it.

The expiry alert existed but went to a mailbox no one reads since the team was reorganised.

Lessons

Went well

  • The alert on checkout errors paged within two minutes
  • The gateway's logs named the failing handshake

Went badly

  • Nothing listed the certificates issued by hand
  • The expiry warning went to a dead mailbox

Got lucky

  • It happened on a weekday morning with the whole team at work
